children: Walt Disney Company (NYSE:DIS) faces a political and regulatory headwind after an FCC early review of eight ABC licenses, which Disney calls retaliation, even as it reshuffles streaming leadership, hires AI and tech talent, and boosts parks promotions and kid-friendly pricing to shore up growth.
: FCC launched an early review of license renewals for eight ABC stations owned by Walt Disney Company (DIS), initiated by Commissioner Brendan Carr; renewals weren't due until October 2028.
: Disney names former Google/YouTube exec Adam Smith chairman of its streaming unit, giving him senior oversight of Disney’s streaming operations and strategy.
: Disney (DIS) closed at about $102.67, down 2.54% intraday with minor after-hours change; traders noted regulatory dispute and political backdrop tied to the price move.
: Disney names Joe Earley president of TV franchise and content strategy. Earley, at Disney since 2019 and former Hulu president, will lead development of Disney Entertainment’s TV franchises.
: Walt Disney (DIS) hired Anand from Character.AI, formerly at Meta and Microsoft, to boost AI, modernize tech, and accelerate Disney+ direct-to-consumer growth—key for user scale and engagement.
: Walt Disney (DIS) says an FCC move was ordered by Trump and views it as retaliation against its news coverage, framing a dispute between Disney’s news unit and the administration.
: Walt Disney Company (DIS) rolled out summer promotions across theme parks and hotels and linked discounted admission to its Disney Visa, reporting increased seasonal attendance.

: Disney (DIS) changed U.S. parks pricing: Disneyland now offers free park hopping for kids 3–9; Disney World added year-round free dining for young children with qualifying room and dining purchases.
